svg.title: One app, several clear boundaries — Masayume
svg.desc: Market reads, authorized trades and server features take different routes. You + your wallet to Shared market reader: reads. Shared market reader to Market data: public facts. You + your wallet to Wallet or bounded key: approves. Wallet or bounded key to Checked order lane: signed intent. Checked order lane to DreamDEX venue: direct order. Checked order lane to Masayume contracts: vault route. Masayume contracts to DreamDEX venue: venue call. You + your wallet to Next server routes: feature request. You + your wallet to Long-running operators: game socket. Next server routes to Configured AI provider: model request. Next server routes to Postgres records: stored records. Long-running operators to Masayume contracts: bounded calls. Long-running operators to Postgres records: decisions + match history. Long-running operators to Configured AI provider: agent read. Solid arrows show actions or recorded data; dashed arrows show reads and display updates. The map describes implementation paths, not a claim that every operator is online.

text.tspan: Market reads, authorized trades and server features take different routes.

g.title: You + your wallet. The browser shows quotes, records your choices and asks for the signatures the selected route needs. Reading a market does not require spending permission. Control and permission: Your wallet authorizes funds and grants. The app does not own your wallet.

text.tspan: Choose a call or a feature

g.title: Shared market reader. The shared reader gets public market facts. Its book coordinator shares a single normalized book per market instead of opening a separate subscription for every screen. Control and permission: Read-only. This runtime has no account or signing key.

Market data. Discovery and history come from the indexer. Chain status and contract facts come from RPC. Watches and the price feed keep market displays current. These are parallel sources. Control and permission: Public data. Stale and failed reads are reported instead of invented.

Wallet or bounded key. A separate signing session keeps the account fixed while an order is prepared and sent. A browser key works only under the owner’s session grant. Control and permission: A delegated key has an actor, expiry, budget and contract-enforced caps.

Checked order lane. The order lane checks the current market, quote, limits, funds and expiry, records intent, sends the order, then checks what filled. A timeout remains unknown until reconciled. Control and permission: The lane uses the selected signing authority. It does not create authority.

DreamDEX venue. The venue order book matches buys and sells. Its market and oracle rules determine the outcome. Direct-wallet trades and Masayume contracts can both reach it. Control and permission: Public on-chain trading and outcome records.

Next server routes. Server routes provide separate conveniences: advisory AI, account linking, bounded gas sponsorship and private-desk requests. These features do not all share one spending model. Control and permission: Server credentials stay server-side. PrivateDesk has a trusted operator.

Long-running operators. Independent actors run strategies, process X mentions, maintain quotes, relay duel rooms and settle eligible contract work. Each actor uses its own configured authority. Control and permission: Operators require the matching grant or contract role. Some calls are permissionless.

Masayume contracts. EventVault, specialist reserves and GameArena manage their own balances and payout rules. PrivateDesk is a separate contract with a stronger desk trust assumption. Control and permission: Contract-specific authority; these balances are not one shared account.

Configured AI provider. Sensei returns advice. The agent model returns a structured side, confidence and reason, which the runner checks against fixed rules before considering execution. Control and permission: The model has no signing tool.

Postgres records. The database stores social activity, X links and receipts, agent decisions, game history and scoreboards. It helps servers resume and show history; it does not decide market payouts. Control and permission: Server-managed records. Several optional features need it to function.

text.tspan: Solid arrows show actions or recorded data; dashed arrows show reads and display updates. The map describes implementation paths,
not a claim that every operator is online.
